newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - Handelsbanken seen posting higher '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Handelsbanken seen posting higher '96 profit.

text.p: Swedish bank Handelsbanken was expected to post a higher profit after credit losses of 6.03 billion crowns for 1996, a Reuters poll of 12 analysts found on Wednesday.
This compared to a pre-tax profit after credit losses of 4.96 billion crowns in 1995. Credit losses amounted to 2.39 billion crowns last year.
Profit forecasts for 1996 varied between 5.91 and 6.21 billion crowns.
In the first nine months of the year the bank reported a profit of 4.52 billion crowns.
Analysts forecast that credit losses in 1996 would be 1.7 billion crowns which gave expectations of a profit before credit losses of 7.7 billion crowns.
The average forecast for a dividend payment was 4.75 crowns a share.
Not all analysts had taken into account Handelsbanken's proposed takeover of mortgage lender Stadshypotek in forecasts for 1997 and 1998.
Those who had made the necessary adjustments expected a profit after credit losses of 6.8 billion crowns on average and 7.3 billion crowns for the two years respectively.
Analysts polled were from Aros, BZW, Carnegie, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Enskilda, Fiba, Handelsbanken, J.P. Morgan, James Capel, Kleinwort Benson, Morgan Stanley, Penser, Swedbank, and Ohman.
Handelsbanken will release its annual result on February 18.
